messages:
release-coordinator: Kicking off hotpin canary for service=web, version=sha:abcd1234. Change window 22:00-23:30 UTC. pin is in place, 10% traffic to canary. Deploy-bot: canary started on 5 hosts. Monitoring hooks enabled.

deploy-bot: canary metrics stream -> p50=120ms p95=480ms error_rate=0.2% 

maria: linking the backout runbook? want the exact steps if we decide to unwind.

release-coordinator: runbook here: https://runbooks.redwood.internal/backout-web-canary-v2 (section 3 = immediate unwind). TL;DR: criteria = (error_rate >= 2.5% for 3m) OR (p95 > 1s for 5m) OR any user-facing 5xx spike. If met -> unpin and route to stable. Also note DB-migration flag: none for this release.

olivia: got it. who will execute the unpin if triggered?

ops-oncall: I'll take the primary action for first 20m. @sam you'll be backup for rollback commands?

sam: yep, I'll be on standby. SHOUT if you need me to run the command.

maria: copy. what's the exact CLI incantation?

sam: use quick-unpin helper: ```
# unpin canary -> route traffic back to stable
rctl deployment unpin --service web --version abcd1234 --reason "canary-backout"
# verify rollout
rctl deployment status --service web --watch
```

release-coordinator: note: if unpin fails or doesn't restore due to a canary-specific config, fallback is to scale down canary infra: ```
rctl scale --service web --env canary --replicas 0
```

deploy-bot: alert: 22:07:16 canary metrics -> p50=130ms p95=1025ms error_rate=3.4% :rotating_light:

maria: ack. that crosses the error threshold (>=2.5% for 3m). initiating unwind per runbook. ops-oncall, take it.

ops-oncall: starting unpin now. running helper.

ops-oncall: executing: rctl deployment unpin --service web --version abcd1234 --reason "automated-canary-backout"

sam: monitoring logs, ready to jump in if ops hits failures.

deploy-bot: action log -> unpin job submitted (id=job-8891). health checks flipping.

ops-oncall: unpin job finished. sanity checks: p95=420ms error_rate=0.15% :white_check_mark:

maria: thanks. can we add a short postmortem note in the release doc? root cause unknown — retry with telemetry toggled off in next patch.

release-coordinator: yes, add to release notes: "Canary v2.3.1 triggered automated backout due to elevated error rate. No DB migrations; rolling revision will be recreated after investigation." Link to incident ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/OPS-1234

sam: also adding the runbook pointer to the ticket and the pin/unpin command we used.

olivia: will we re-run canary later tonight or wait for ops triage?

release-coordinator: hold — ops to triage for 45m. if root cause is config, we may re-push a patched canary in the next change window.

deploy-bot: deploy summary -> canary started 22:00, backout triggered 22:07, full restore by 22:12.

maria: closing thread for now. great coordination. :handshake:
